The FOMC held the target range at 5.25–5.50% and reaffirmed QT, emphasizing the need for greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably to 2%. Incorporating the Beige Book (prepared January 8, 2024) tempers the statement’s “solid pace” characterization: districts reported mixed-to-flat economic activity with a reported decrease in manufacturing, softer firm expectations, and interest rates limiting auto sales and real estate deals, though some contacts note the prospect of falling rates. Labor markets are loosening at the margin—easing hiring challenges, lower turnover, and wage growth characterized as moderate in Boston and San Francisco—consistent with easing inflation pressures. Layering in the SLOOS, banks have tightened standards (notably for CRE) with weaker C&I loan demand, citing risk, liquidity/capital, and secondary-market conditions; this credit headwind supports further disinflation but raises downside growth risks. Netting these factors, staying restrictive is appropriate, and the outlook is mildly positive but more guarded than the statement alone implies.
